clue.text: A decent return from industry? Not much it is!

definitions.text: A decent return from industry? Not much it is!

parts.words: A decent return from industry? Not much it is!
parts.note: a 'decent return' sounds like a fair reward for hard work, but 'decent' is read as merely respectable and the exclamation admits the sum is small

explanation.surface: A worker grumbles that honest toil earns very little.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as praise for a good return; the second half undercuts it, so the phrase wanted is pay that is decent in the sense of unassuming rather than generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Modest earnings are respectable but small, a fair return for work that is still not much money.

clue.text: Sort of cocktail I swallow first, apparently

indicators.note: the clue says the swallow comes first, so its synonym is placed ahead of the I

parts.note: the house martin is a bird of the swallow family

explanation.surface: Someone describes how they drink a cocktail, gulping it down at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like a verb about drinking; it is the bird, a martin. 'I swallow first' tells you to write the bird before I.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a well-known gin and vermouth mixed drink.

clue.text: Treated as a god in ascent or decline

indicators.note: in a down light the word is read upwards or downwards, and either way gives the same letters

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A figure is worshipped whether their fortunes rise or fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascent or decline' sounds like rising and falling fortunes, but in a down entry it means reading up or down: the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: To deify is to make into or worship as a deity, so the past tense means worshipped like a divinity.

clue.text: A steward seen to clash when in disarray

indicators.note: disarray is disorder, so the letters of the two words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A household servant is seen to quarrel when things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when in disarray' is the anagram signal; 'to' between the two fodder words is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A seneschal was the official in charge of a medieval great house, a senior household manager.

clue.text: Welsh giant holding an old penny flag?

indicators.note: holding means the flower name keeps the coin abbreviation inside it

parts.note: the yellow flag is a wild iris
D (from Latin denarius) was the abbreviation for a penny before British decimal coinage in 1971

explanation.surface: A Welsh giant clutches a coin and a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is the plant, not a banner. Idris is the legendary giant of Cader Idris, a mountain in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: In Welsh legend Idris Gawr was a huge figure said to sit on the mountain Cader Idris.

clue.text: Wedge-shaped rod with neat inset

indicators.note: inset means placed within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a cue is the rod used in billiards and snooker

explanation.surface: A tidy rod is described as having a wedge-shaped insert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inset' signals the container; 'with' is a link. 'Rod' is the snooker cue, not a fishing rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuneate is a botanical and anatomical term for something tapering like a wedge, from Latin cuneus.

clue.text: Maudlin Frenchman given a new whisk

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, the French title for a man

indicators.note: new signals the letters of the following words in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A sentimental Frenchman is handed a new kitchen whisk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' sits between A and WHISK; their letters are rearranged to AWKISH and put after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly sentimental, the same tearful excess as maudlin.

clue.text: Rival play group fighting against pretentiousness?

explanation.surface: A rival theatre company sets itself against showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: opposing as fighting against, and side as airs or swank.
explanation.definitionFit: The team you play against is your rivals; side also means swagger or affectation, so the phrase also means resisting airs.

clue.text: Some haven to which no one returns

parts.note: a port is a haven for ships

indicators.note: returns signals reading the words for no and one backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A harbour to which no one ever comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns both short words together, giving ION; 'to which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a part or share of something, as is some of it.

clue.text: Restoration novel in authentic setting

indicators.note: the word for novel goes in the word for authentic
setting means the authentic word frames the other like a jewel in its mount

parts.note: authentic means real
novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: A Restoration-era novel is placed in a genuine period setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Restoration' looks like the historical period; it means renewal. 'Novel' is the adjective new, not a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A restoration is a revival or repair, bringing something back to fresh condition.

clue.text: A lot on one's plate, possibly

definitions.text: A lot on one's plate, possibly

parts.words: A lot on one's plate, possibly
parts.note: the idiom of having a lot on one's plate means being busy, but here it is taken literally as a big serving of food

explanation.surface: Someone is overwhelmed with work.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous portion of food piled on a dish is literally plenty on the plate.

clue.text: Starts with nothing before rising in agony

indicators.note: before places the zero ahead of the next piece

parts.note: O, the zero, stands for nothing

indicators.note: agony suggests writhing and twisting, so the letters of the word are contorted

explanation.surface: Someone begins with nothing before getting up in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in agony' is the anagram signal, making RIGINS; 'before' puts the zero ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Origins are beginnings, the points where things start.

clue.text: On hot days a herd is disposed to seek such conditions

definitions.text: On hot days a herd is disposed to seek such conditions

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cattle in a heatwave head for cooler spots.
explanation.walkthrough: A HERD IS is rearranged; the whole clue also describes cattle looking for less sunny places.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals in heat seek places with more cover from the sun, which are less sunny spots.

clue.text: Epic investment story held back by the dailies

indicators.note: held back means the letters run backwards inside the words
investment is read as being clothed or contained, so the story is wrapped within the words

explanation.surface: Newspapers sit on a story about a big investment.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'the dailies' backwards gives seiliadeht, which contains the answer; 'story' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's poem of the Trojan War is the classic Greek epic.

clue.text: Piece of forgery that could bring one luck

definitions.text: Piece of forgery that could bring one luck

parts.words: Piece of forgery that could bring one luck
parts.note: forgery suggests faking documents, but here it is the work of a blacksmith's forge, and the item is a lucky charm

explanation.surface: A faked document that might pay off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forgery' is read as forge work, metal shaped by a smith.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith shapes these iron shoes, and one hung over a door is a traditional good-luck token.

clue.text: A mac to knock about in on top of the house?

indicators.note: in a down light 'on' puts the first piece above the next
about means the knock word goes around the small word

parts.note: to rap is to knock
the roof is the top of a house

explanation.surface: A raincoat to wear while knocking about up on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container, giving RAINP; in a down light 'on' sets it above the house's top. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mackintosh is a waterproof coat, so it can be called a rainproof.

clue.text: American soldier restraining a scurrilous Italian revolutionary

indicators.note: restraining means the soldier holds the other words in

parts.note: GI is the slang name for a US soldier
ribald means coarse and scurrilous

explanation.surface: A US soldier holds back a foul-mouthed Italian rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restraining' signals the container: the American soldier holds the rest of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the Redshirts in the fight to unify Italy in the 19th century.

clue.text: Unprosaic composition on a rude development

indicators.note: a development reworks material, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A verse piece grows out of a vulgar idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Development' is the music term for working over a theme; here it reorders ON A RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain, so it is poetry rather than prose.

clue.text: Vigorously chides creatures that buzz round desert

indicators.note: round means the insects surround the other word

parts.note: bees are insects that buzz
to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Someone scolds buzzing insects circling a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a noun, sand; it is the verb, to rat. 'round' signals that the insects surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: To berate is to scold angrily.

clue.text: A series that needs to be pushed along?

definitions.text: that needs to be pushed along?

explanation.surface: Something that keeps going only when it is pushed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a bicycle, which you push with the pedals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is a set of events or works in order, and also a bike, moved by pushing on the pedals.

clue.text: Cold game beginning to turn up at the edges?

definitions.text: beginning to turn up at the edges?

explanation.surface: An icy match where the corners start to lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Curling is a sport played on ice, sliding stones toward a target.
explanation.definitionFit: The sport with stones and brooms is played on ice; paper or leaves bending upward at the rims are rolling up.

clue.text: A time-serving code-breaker!

parts.note: a code-breaker sounds like a cryptographer, but here it is one who broke the legal code and is serving time in jail

explanation.surface: A long-serving cryptographer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time-serving' is literal: serving a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner sentenced for a crime has broken the law and is doing time.

clue.text: Passes over various regions

indicators.note: various suggests diverse forms, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Travel through several areas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passes over' looks like flying over places; it means overlooks.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass over something is to disregard it, to take no notice of it.

clue.text: Apollo's first show?

parts.note: Apollo sounds like a theatre or space mission, but he is the Greek sun god, and his first appearance of the day is dawn

explanation.surface: The opening night of a theatre called the Apollo.
explanation.walkthrough: Apollo is the sun god in Greek myth, so his first show is the sun appearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is when the sun first rises above the horizon.

clue.text: Vegetarian fare making loveless parson turn sanctimon ous

indicators.note: love is zero in tennis, so loveless means without the O
turn means the short word for sanctimonious is reversed

parts.note: pi is a slang shortening of pious, meaning sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A dull parson becomes a self-righteous vegetarian.
explanation.walkthrough: PARSON loses O to give PARSN; PI turned gives IP. 'Making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsnips are root vegetables, food that a vegetarian would eat.

clue.text: Turn out on Merseyside?

parts.note: to evert is to turn inside out

explanation.surface: People turn out in Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a district of Liverpool on Merseyside, home of Everton football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a part of Liverpool and a football club in north-west England.

clue.text: No one on Page One disseminates it? That's what you think!

indicators.note: disseminates means scatters, so the letters of these words are spread into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor wonders whether a front-page story is just a view.
explanation.walkthrough: NO, I, ON, P, I are rearranged; 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or belief is what someone thinks.

clue.text: Strikes rather than give in?

parts.note: strikes suggests industrial action, but here it means hitting blows instead of surrendering

explanation.surface: Workers walk out rather than accept terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' reads as a noun for walkouts; it is a verb for landing blows.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist strongly instead of yielding is to battle on, hitting back.
